**Grammar change (`arch.langium`):** The old regex `/\[[\w ]+\]/` is extended to also allow double-quoted and single-quoted strings (with escape sequence support via `\\.`). That's the right direction.

**Value converter (`valueConverter.ts`):** The old code stripped `[` and `]`. The new code strips `"`, `'`, `[`, and `]` globally with `/["'[\]]/g`. This is the problematic part — it removes every quote character anywhere in the string.

**Potential failure cases I can identify:**
1. `["It's ready"]` — double-quoted title containing an apostrophe. The grammar allows this (single quotes are fine inside double-quoted strings per `[^"\\]`). But the converter strips all `'`, yielding `Its ready`.
2. `['He said "hi"']` — single-quoted title containing double quotes. Same problem; yields `He said hi`.
3. `["say \"hello\""]` — escaped quotes inside. The grammar's `\\.` allows this. The converter strips all `"` *and* leaves the backslash, yielding `say \hello\` instead of `say "hello"`.

**Tests:** All four tests use simple single-word labels that would be equally valid unquoted with the old grammar. None of them exercise special characters or embedded quotes, so they don't catch any of the above bugs.
